title: Activation lifecycle mapping and cross-team handoffs - working notes
content:
Purpose
---
This is a working artifact to map the full activation lifecycle for LLM-driven feature rollouts (canaries, micro-exposures, A/B) and to make explicit the cross-team handoffs, signals, and quick-abort criteria. Intended audience: product leads, SRE/oncall, serving runtime, console/rollouts, solutions eng.

Why this doc (notes to self)
- Lots of rollout incidents trace back to ambiguous ownership during the activation window (who owns prefix-cache flushes? who flips the route?).
- We need an explicit lifecycle that is machine-readable later (but for now, human checklist).
- Focus on minimizing blast radius while giving product owners predictable observability.

High-level activation lifecycle (stages)
1) Design & hypothesis (product)
   - Hypothesis statement + acceptance criteria (quality & business metrics)
   - Minimum test prompts / eval prompts pinned
   - Target cohorts and slices defined

2) Preflight (multi-team prep)
   - Infra: capacity plan (tokens/sec expected), warmup plan for KV caches
   - Runtime: model variant pin, quantization profile, fallback models defined
   - Observability: dashboards + alert thresholds created and shared
   - Security/Compliance check (if enterprise/private)

3) Canary activation (low traffic)
   - Start with deterministic microcohort (e.g., 0.1% traffic, internal beta users)
   - Validation signals: latency p50/p95, error-rate, perplexity drift vs baseline, quality evaluation sweep (daily)
   - Ownership: oncall SRE + product owner watch window (duration = min 2h or 2k requests)

4) Ramp (incremental exposure)
   - Step increases with hold windows and explicit sign-offs
   - Automated rollback triggers (see quick-abort section below)

5) Post-rollout monitoring & deprecation window
   - Continue quality and cost telemetry for N days (N depends on feature risk)
content_2:
Signals we care about (operational + quality)
- Operational:
  - request_success_rate (95th percentile)
  - downstream_error_rate (application exceptions triggered by responses)
  - model_latency_p50/p95/p99 (token-incremental and overall)
  - GPU utilization, queueing time, rejection_rate
  - per-request cost estimate delta vs baseline
- Quality:
  - automated eval score (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity/LLM-eval metric as applicable)
  - hallucination-count proxy: name-entity hallucination delta 
  - human-labeled false-positive/negative rates (sampled)

Quick-abort and rollback heuristics (conservative defaults)
- Immediate abort (AUTO): any of the following
  - total_request_failure_rate increases > 3x baseline AND absolute > 2% for 10 min
  - model_latency_p95 increases > 2x baseline for 15 min AND user-visible errors spike
  - critical safety classifier fires on > 0.3% of sampled responses in 1h window
- Soft rollback / pause (MANUAL):
  - eval-quality drop > 7% on pinned prompt set over 24h
  - cost-per-successful-response increases > 30% for 24h without business uplift

Who does what (hand-off matrix, informal)
- Product owner: hypothesis, target slices, rollout speed decision, final go/no-go
- Console team: dashboard templating, rollout toggle wiring, feature flag exposure logic
- Serving runtime / infra: provision capacity, model pin, warming KV cache, fallback routes
- SRE oncall: operational watch for first 6 hours and can trigger auto-abort on infra signals
- Solutions engineering / CS: watch for early customer feedback (esp for Dedicated/Private kits)

Operational Playbook (checklist)
- Preflight checklist (done before canary)
  - [ ] Create rollout feature flag in console and map cohorts
  - [ ] Create the per-model dashboard: latency, errors, cost, eval-score
  - [ ] Confirm model variants and fallback mapping in routing policy (include region fallback)
  - [ ] Warm cache (script link below) and verify latency baseline
  - [ ] Add brief runbook stub in PagerDuty escalation notes

- Canary activation checklist
  - [ ] Flip flag to internal cohort (0.1%) and note timestamp
  - [ ] Run evaluation job against pinned prompts (baseline vs new)
  - [ ] Handshake in #rollout-coord (post message with timestamp, brief metrics snapshot)
  - [ ] SRE acknowledges and starts 2h watch

- Ramp checklist (each step)
  - [ ] Verify last hold-window metrics meet acceptance
  - [ ] Increase exposure (e.g., 0.1 -> 1 -> 5 -> 20%) and record note
  - [ ] If any signal breaches, follow quick-abort heuristics

Example rollout schedule (timeline template)
- Day 0: Preflight and capacity warmup
- Day 1: Internal canary (0.1%) - 4h watch + eval sweep at end of window
- Day 2: External beta (1%) - 24h watch
- Day 3: Ramp to 5% if green, extend evaluation
- Day 5: 20% with continued monitoring, review cost impact
- Day 10: Full exposure or gated by org decision

Sample SQL snippets for quick signals (placeholders)
- Recent request error rate (30m rolling):
  SELECT bin, count(*) as reqs, sum(is_error::int) as errors, (sum(is_error::int)/count(*)) as err_rate
  FROM requests
  WHERE model_variant = 'v-new' AND timestamp > now() - interval '30 minutes'
  GROUP BY bin ORDER BY bin DESC LIMIT 10;

- Sample eval aggregation (daily):
  SELECT prompt_id, avg(eval_score) as mean_score, pctile_disc(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY eval_score) as median_score
  FROM eval_runs
  WHERE run_tag = 'preflight-2025-09' AND timestamp > now() - interval '1 day'
  GROUP BY prompt_id;

Open questions / things to resolve
- How do we standardize a single "exposure" signal across Hosted/Dedicated/Private where metric availability differs? (put on backlog with infra)
- Should we add an automated verifier that checks KV cache hit-rate after warmup and blocks ramp if below threshold?
- Fine-grained risk budgets by business area: product wants fast ramp but payments-related features must be conservative. Do we encode product-specific risk budgets in console?

Small experiments I want to run / TODOs
- Build a reusable dashboard template that includes: token-cost delta, eval-score drift, per-slice latency, last rollback reason (text field). (owner: Lena, due: 2025-12-15)
- Prototype a stepper UI in console that commits ramp steps and records sign-offs (low-effort, product-UX spike). (owner: Marcus)
- Add an "activation metadata" manifest to rollouts (JSON schema) that can be versioned with PRs (tracks hypothesis, pinned prompts, stoplight thresholds).

References and quick links
- Confluence: rollouts/activation-lifecycle-map (design doc)
- Jira: RL-982 (activation metadata schema), RL-990 (dashboard template)
notes: Informal working doc — expect incomplete sentences, TODOs, and questions. Will iterate into a proper playbook once we validate the lifecycle on two features.
